title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC0LA_0RD1RB_1RE0RF_0LA1LE_---0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC0LA_0RD1RB_1RE0RF_0LA1LE_---0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The tape is a block (100)^n followed by blocks of ones separated by 00, almost all of length 6j+1 (7, 13, 19, ...) and grouped by length: a counter with one digit per length, rewritten as the head sweeps the tape. The rule of one sweep has not been extracted, so there is no map to iterate and no heuristic. Direct simulation: no halt in 1011 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 30,887 cells have been visited and 19,819 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.065).

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.07×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 3.07×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.01×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 1,600 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: The counter's rule
claims.text: How one sweep changes the block multiplicities and the (100) block; see the README's For later.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: Block lengths of the counter; its rule is not decoded.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.01×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: Blocks of ones of lengths 7, 13, 19, ...
html:
Read left to right, the tape is (100)^n followed by blocks of ones separated by 00. Almost all have length 6j+1 and they come grouped by length, in increasing order, with a few short blocks between the groups. At the right end, at three moments (n, then the block lengths, 7^54 for 54 blocks of length 7):

step  1,153,586  n=76   5 7^54 5 1^2 15 19^11 17 1 5 29 31 13 29 1^2 7 3 1
step  7,772,173  n=75   5 7^123 1 11 13^30 11 1^2 17 19^18 1 11 23 25^6 1 11 29 31^2 35^2 1^2 41^2 1^2 15 5
step 20,110,251  n=140  3 7^220 5 1^2 11 13^26 1 5 17 19^42 7 1 21 25^5 13 29 31^7 35 37 7 1 39 23 7 1 3 1^2 13 1

It behaves like a counter with one digit per block length. The head sweeps the whole tape again and again, adding a few cells each time, so the width grows like the square root of the step count; on the way it rewrites the short blocks between groups.

sections.heading: Not known
html:
The machine halts only in F reading 0 (D reads a 1 with a 0 to its right). No rule for the counter is known yet, so there is neither a map to iterate nor a heuristic. Direct simulation: no halt in 1011 steps.

Next steps (README, For later): record the block list at every sweep, find the rule at one group boundary with symbolic simulation, then write and check the counter map.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.065).
After 109 steps the tape spans 30,887 cells (22,712 left of the start, 457 right), with a density of 1s of 0.642.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
